experiment: GPT-2 B1 bridge: TopK k=64 + beta*L1, standard and bypass conditions, 5 seeds, beta in {0, 0.03, 0.1, 0.3}

training.store: v3 gpt2_wikitext store: first 5M tokens of WikiText-103-v1 train, one document per 128-token sequence, padding excluded
training.centering: x - train mean (raw scale, no rescaling)
training.init_seed: torch.manual_seed(seed) and v3 BaseSAE tied init with Generator(seed)
training.decoder: rows renormalized to unit norm after every Adam step
training.bypass: x - (x.v1) v1 with the train PC1 before encoding (bypass condition only)

protocol.alive: calibration-alive = fired at least once on the calibration split. The bridge uses the FROZEN alive ids from the grid evaluator (identical sets, checked); fresh_alive is the bridge re-count on its own bfloat16 calibration pass.
protocol.importance: signed single-feature zero-ablation dCE vs the unmodified model ("model" baseline), token-weighted over the ranking split; every calibration-alive feature evaluated (no screen)
protocol.top50: top_ids: the 50 calibration-alive features with the largest dCE on the named split; ties broken by feature index
protocol.sharing: for source seed a and each other seed b in the same (condition, beta): best = max over b's calibration-alive decoder rows of the signed cosine with a's decoder row. top50_pairwise_sharing(a) = fraction of (other seed, selected feature) pairs with best >= 0.7. Reported sharing = mean over the 5 source seeds. dictwide uses all of a's calibration-alive features instead of the top 50.
protocol.l0: bridge fidelity(): total nonzero codes over the split's valid tokens / number of valid tokens (no row cap)
protocol.fvu: fvu_total = sum||x - xhat||^2 / sum||x - mean_eval||^2; fvu_content (fvu_perp) = same on the complement of the train PC1; w1 = PC1 share of evaluation variance; identity fvu_total = w1*fvu_pc1 + (1-w1)*fvu_content holds to <3e-18
protocol.uncertainty: sharing: article-resampled paired bootstrap (bridge paired_contrasts, ~1000 draws). L0/FVU/alive: across the 5 seeds (mean, SD, Student-t 95%); beta effects are PAIRED by seed (identical init seed and data order across beta).
